previous_last_sync.summary: The repository README now presents the public Capoworks ECU on-demand firmware builder, including how to sign in, select a board, choose opt-in modules and table dimensions, download the matching firmware image and generated TunerStudio INI, and the limit of six builds per user per day. The existing on-demand firmware build wiki page is updated to describe the public builder alongside the manual workflow, with the same profile rules, artifact pairing, and safety boundaries.

decisions.rationale: The repository README now advertises the public Capoworks ECU on-demand firmware builder at capoworks.undo.it/firmware and adds a section describing the user flow: sign in, select a supported board, choose opt-in modules and table dimensions, then download the matching firmware image and generated TunerStudio INI. It also states a limit of six builds per user per day. The on-demand firmware build wiki page is updated so readers can use the public builder as well as the manual GitHub Actions workflow, while keeping the same profile rules, the requirement to treat firmware and INI as one matching pair, and the warning that a successful build is not engine or hardware validation.

last_sync.summary: Anti-lag now requires a valid driver throttle-intent signal before it can arm, and the anti-lag ETB target addition is applied only when anti-lag is enabled and the accelerator-pedal reading is valid. The ETB pedal-target page is updated to describe these conditions.

decisions.rationale: Anti-lag arming now fails closed: if the driver throttle-intent signal is missing or non-finite, the anti-lag throttle condition is false and anti-lag does not activate, even if RPM, coolant, and switch conditions are met. The anti-lag ETB target addition is also gated on anti-lag being enabled and on a valid, finite accelerator-pedal reading, so a stale active flag or a failed pedal sensor no longer adds ALSEtbAdd to the throttle target. No tune migration is required; existing anti-lag tunes keep their settings. Check that the pedal and throttle-intent sensors are calibrated and healthy before relying on anti-lag, and treat a lost pedal signal as an anti-lag inhibit rather than a fault to tune around.
